item.title: U.S. and Iran Send Conflicting Signals on Peace Prospects
item.summary: President Trump said talks were underway. A top Iranian official denied that, while other Iranians said messages were being traded through intermediaries.

item.title: Sidelined by War With Iran, Gaza Residents Remain in Limbo
item.summary: The new war has led to panic buying and a surge in food prices for Gazans as they try to recover from Israel’s two-year offensive against Hamas.

item.title: A Choice of Deadly Drones Is Only a Few Clicks Away for Ukrainian Troops
item.summary: Ukraine has created online marketplaces to let units select their own drones, a break from generations of standardized and centralized weapons procurement.

item.title: Caught Between Two Conflicts, Afghans Flee Iran
item.summary: The war in Iran is choking off Afghanistan’s main economic lifeline and has forced at least 70,000 Afghan workers and students there back home to a nation embroiled in another conflict.

item.title: On Beirut’s Waterfront, Loss Meets Life, and Luxury, Amid War
item.summary: Thousands displaced by Israeli strikes on Lebanon’s capital now shelter along the promenade hugging the Mediterranean Sea. They share it with joggers, cyclists and dog walkers, alongside dizzying displays of wealth.

item.title: Trump Sours on British Leader Over Iran War: ‘What If Donald Shouts at Me?’
item.summary: President Trump once called Prime Minister Keir Starmer a friend. But Mr. Starmer’s decision not to join the attacks on Iran has led to merciless mocking by the president.

item.title: How North Korea’s Kim Jong-un Is Using the Iran War to Justify His Nuclear Arsenal
item.summary: He delivered a lengthy speech at his country’s rubber-stamp Parliament, declaring that his nuclear power will shield his country from American hostility.

item.title: Trump Delays Threat to Iran, but War Negotiations Are in Early Stage
item.summary: President Trump postponed his threat to strike power plants in Iran, citing “productive conversations” with the Iranians. But officials said the talks were in an early stage and not substantive.

item.title: Taiwan Debates Military Spending as Choices Over U.S. and China Loom
item.summary: Tensions in the opposition Nationalist Party could surface this week as lawmakers argue over additional defense funding intended to counter Beijing’s growing might.

item.title: Canada May Need to Lean on the US as Military Threats in the Arctic Rise
item.summary: For the past seven decades, Canada has been the junior partner in a military agreement with the United States to protect the Canadian Arctic.
